What Zelda analyzed The work behind this report — counted, not estimated. 12 Pages analyzed 12 Sections searched 2 Categories analyzed Business Model & Growth Analysis Insufficient disclosed data to describe the business model. No product statement, no revenue statement, and no problem statement were extracted from the document. While the company is categorized as a software company at Series A stage [P1, P2] and the traction figures reference bots and messages [S1, S2, S3], no information about pricing, monetization mechanism, customer acquisition, or growth drivers appears in the extracted evidence. It is not possible to characterize how ManyChat generates revenue or what drives expansion. Information Readiness Score: 10/100 Present: • Traction metrics: 140,000+ bots and 500M messages, on a slide headed 'Traction by Apr-16' [S1, S2] • A second messages figure (500M messages/month) on a separate page [S3] • Funding raised figure as narrated by Pitch Deck Hunt: $23.1M [S4] • Stage (Series A) and sector (Software) from profile [P1, P2] Needs Validation: • Measurement basis of messages metric: cumulative vs. monthly [C2, C3] • External confirmation of funding raised [C1] • Revenue, burn rate, and financial statements • Team composition and credentials • Problem and solution description • Product description • Market size and competitive landscape • Risk factors • Use of proceeds Next evidence to supply: Audited or reviewed financial statements showing revenue, gross margin, and cash position, alongside a reconciled explanation of whether the 500M messages figure is cumulative or monthly. Supported Points The company states 140,000+ bots had been deployed, as shown on a slide headed 'Traction by Apr-16' [S1]. This is a self-reported figure that was not independently verified [C4], but it provides a concrete scale reference for bot adoption at that point in time. Pitch Deck Hunt lists $23.1M as the total amount raised [S4]. While this could not be confirmed by external evidence [C1], it establishes the fundraising narrative the company has put forward and sets a baseline for diligence on capital history. Open Concerns The core usage metric — 500M messages — is stated with two different measurement bases in the same deck: without an interval on page 10 ('Traction by Apr-16') [C3, S2] and as a monthly figure on page 12 [C2, S3]. This inconsistency has not been reconciled and must be clarified before the figure can be interpreted, because the difference between a cumulative total and a monthly rate is material to assessing the company's scale. No revenue, burn, or financial data of any kind was extracted from the document. For a company described as Series A [P1], the absence of any financial disclosure makes it impossible to evaluate commercial progress, capital efficiency, or how the $23.1M (per Pitch Deck Hunt) narrated as raised [S4] has been deployed. No team information was extracted from the document. At the Series A stage [P1], the absence of founder and leadership credentials removes one of the primary inputs to investment assessment. No problem, product, or market information was extracted from the document. Without these, the context for interpreting the traction figures [S1, S2, S3] — whether the addressable market supports the scale implied, and whether the product has structural advantages — cannot be evaluated. What Would Change the Picture The single most important missing piece of evidence is a dated financial statement — at minimum a P&L showing revenue and gross margin alongside a cash balance and monthly burn rate — which would allow assessment of whether the self-reported traction [S1, S2, S3] is translating into commercial scale and how long the company can operate on the capital narrated as raised [S4].
